articles.title: IDB to Involve Indigenous Groups in Ife Strategic Development Plan
articles.summary: Individuals, families, clubs and associations will join stakeholder sessions to shape a plan guiding investment across IfeLand for the next 25 years.
articles.body:
The Ife Development Board (IDB) plans to involve sensitive indigenous groups in the Ife Strategic Development Plan. Individuals, families, clubs and associations will participate in stakeholder sessions to discuss the proposed plan.

This 25-year Strategic Development Plan aims to guide the mobilisation and investment of resources for IfeLand's growth.

Presented at the May 2026 board meeting, the chairman of the committee, Dr. Yomi Layinka, explained the integrated community development strategy for Ile-Ife. The plan stems from various submissions and documents, including Osun State development initiatives and Vision 2050.

Key areas of focus include agriculture, tourism, and human capacity development.

The presentation highlighted potential funding sources and recommended developing a stakeholder engagement roadmap, to ensure broad participation, consensus building, and ownership among relevant community groups.

Responding to Dr. Layinka's request for a dedicated session to thoroughly review the proposal before wider circulation, board members agreed to circulate it internally first.

The meeting resolved to share the document with the Ife Community Trust Fund and the Ife Board of Trustees. The committee will then prepare presentation materials — including slides and draft Strategic Development Plan extracts — and design a stakeholder engagement schedule.

articles.title: Adefaye Launches Ife Community Website
articles.summary: The Board's first-ever community website goes live, built to educate, inform, and draw visitors from around the world to Ile-Ife.
articles.body:
President of Ife Development Board, Gbenga Adefaye, has announced the establishment of the first community website for Ife indigenes and tourists.

Adefaye, who is also the Provost of the Nigerian Institute of Journalism, said the creation of the digital resource fulfils one of the priorities of his administration of the Board. He said the digital resource shall educate, inform and attract visitors worldwide to Ile-Ife, the ancestral home of the Yoruba.

Operating with the domain name ife-development-board.org, the website features daily updates of major developmental projects and programmes improving the lives of residents. A section titled "Explore Ife" provides real-life pictures of historic and interesting places in the city.

The site went live at midnight on July 1, 2026, and has been receiving positive reviews for making it easy for visitors to navigate its pages.

Reviewing the site, World Bank Consultant Dr. Akin Awofolaju said: "The new IDB website is a commendable effort and represents a major step forward in projecting a modern digital image for the Ife Development Board. The platform demonstrates a clear intention to position IDB as a forward-looking organization focused on community development, strategic planning, and stakeholder engagement. The clean design, responsive layout, and modern web architecture indicate that considerable thought and effort have gone into the project. The website succeeds in creating a professional first impression, but with several strategic enhancements it could evolve from a good informational website into an exceptional community engagement and development platform."

Opeyemi Eludiora, Chief Executive Officer of CrystalTech Limited, the consultants on the website project, described the intended user experience: "Through our social media handles, we would have alert messages diverting people to the website to read up. We also have event alerts, and history and projects alerts. As a user, I will want to see things about Ife before seeing the development, and the landing page has shown that. I will want to get familiar with the website."

The chairman of the IDB Website Committee, Kehinde Bamigbetan, commended the consultants for a job well done, adding that content management will be driven by messaging designed to reach the appropriate target audience. "They took the brief seriously and turned out a fantastic website that is culturally stimulating and aesthetically captivating," he said.
